verdicts.flaw_description: Rainfall in each block's season 'ran to roughly double the year before' and 'every block lay in open ground, taking rain as it fell', so a doubling of water supply is an alternative cause that applies to all four blocks; the 0.4-0.7 t/ha gains cannot be attributed to the drip line.

In two of the four cases the outcome is measured before the inhaler was started: case one 'started 4 March' but counted attacks 'by 28 February', and case three 'started 5 September' but counted 'by 30 August'. An effect recorded before the intervention began cannot be caused by it.

'Class sizes at each school fell by half from the year before, and every logged class took its English lessons as one whole group', so every class experienced a halved class size at the same time as the program; the 5-9 point comprehension gains are equally explained by the class-size cut.

The claim is about board defects but the measured quantity is 'mean void area' (down 4-7 percent), a continuous process metric, not a defect count or defect rate; the report even says the runs were 'graded at electrical test', yet no defect grading result is reported.
